newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 11.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Tuesday:
* Two black men were convicted for the 1991 fatal stabbing of a Hasidic Jew during the racial violence in Crown Heights, Brooklyn.

* A civil jury in California ordered O.J. Simpson to pay $12.5 million in punitive damages for the death of his ex-wife, Nicole Simpson, and another $12.5 million for the death of her friend, Ronald Goldman.

* The New York State Board of Regents removed all but one of the 19 trustees of Adelphi University, citing the excessive pay they gave the university's president and their failure to let faculty participate in the school's governance.
* The National Football League brokered a deal freeing coach Bill Parcells from his contract with the New England Patriots and allowing him to immediately sign on as head coach of the New York Jets.

* Scientists have concluded that a child's footprint, bone tools and other arteficts found in Chile point to human habitation of the New World 12,500 years ago, 1,300 years earlier than previously thought.

* The U.S. Army suspended its highest-ranking enlisted officer, Gene McKinney, who also served on an Army sexual harassment review panel, while it investigates a female soldier's allegations that he assaulted her in a hotel room.

* Althought it remains the world's fourth-biggest industrial power, France is facing a crisis of political and cultural identity, and its economy is challenged by swelling unemployment and near-stagnant growth.
* House Republican leaders decided to postpone any further action on a constitutional amendment to balance the Federal budget.
